13f_amend.why: 13F-HR/A. `amendmentType` decides whether the amendment REPLACES the original's holdings or ADDS to them; getting it wrong either doubles a portfolio or erases most of it. (filed 2025-08-14, period 2025-03-31)

13f_post.why: 13F-HR FILED on or after 2023-01-03, so its values are whole dollars under Release 34-95148. Paired with the pre-cutover fixture, this is what makes the unit rule falsifiable. (filed 2026-08-14, period 2026-06-30)

13f_pre.why: 13F-HR filed BEFORE 2023-01-03, so its values are thousands. Without this half the unit rule is an untested constant. (filed 2022-11-14, period 2022-09-30)

atom_getcurrent.why: parse_current_filings_atom fixture. 100 entries collapse to 49 distinct accessions because SEC emits one entry per filer ROLE (Reporting / Issuer / Subject / Filed by) — a detector that does not dedupe on the accession publishes the same filing up to four times. Captured by an earlier probe under the same User-Agent, so it cost this run nothing.

companyfacts_aapl.why: facts_from_companyfacts_json fixture, and the source of Apple's 10-K accession via the `accn` on its own facts. Also the fixture that proves `frame` survives our parser — edgartools' own parser drops it.

companyfacts_short_history.why: A 2025 IPO, so FEWER THAN FIVE fiscal years. Decision 5 says a short-history filer must yield everything it has and raise nothing; that is only falsifiable against a filer that actually has a short history.

daily_index_20220214.why: parse_daily_index fixture AND the source of a legacy `SC 13G` accession. 2022-02-14 is simultaneously the Q4-2021 13F deadline and the annual 13G deadline, so a single day's index carries both populations and no second request is needed.

efts_8k_search.why: parse_efts_response fixture. `_source` carries `ciks` as an ARRAY and has no `form_type` at all; the field is `form`. Also the source of the 8-K accession, via the only two hits whose `items` array contains '2.02'. Captured by an earlier probe under the same User-Agent.

eightk_bundle.why: 8-K carrying Item 2.02 (results of operations) and 9.01, with an EX-99.1 press release. Accession came free from the already captured EFTS response, whose `items` array names 2.02 outright — so no request was spent hunting for an earnings 8-K.

form4_bundle.why: Insider parsing: derivative rows, footnotes and the `equitySwapInvolved` element. Accession came free from the Atom page; picked by its 13 KB size against 8 KB for its siblings, which is a derivative table.

form4_derivative_bundle.why: The derivative half of insider parsing — underlyingSecurity, underlyingShares, exercisePrice, exerciseDate, expirationDate — six schema columns the Jefferies Form 4 leaves entirely untested, plus the `4/A` amendment path. Chosen as the largest ownership filing on the Atom page (23 KB against 13 KB), which is a derivative table.

schedule13d_bundle.why: A post-2024-12-18 `SCHEDULE 13D` — structured XML, so has_structured_data is True and percent/voting/dispositive fields exist. Accession came free from the Atom page.

schedule13g_legacy.why: A pre-mandate `SC 13G` — HTML only. Proves has_structured_data is False and that the adapter still recovers identities rather than raising, so a 2019 filing's null percentOfClass reads as 'not machine-readable' and never as 'zero'.

submissions_berkshire.why: parse_submissions_json fixture. Berkshire is chosen over a pure operating company because one filer's history has to supply the 13F trio (post-2023, pre-2023, amendment) as well as the paging `filings.files[]` references, and Berkshire files all four.

tenk_bundle_aapl.why: statements_from_bundle fixture — the standardization path, with hand-verified revenue and net income. Apple because its numbers are the ones anyone can check against the filing.
